Subject: Integration: VPC endpoints & private connectivity follow-up

Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we all have the same context.

Recap: FastRetail is evaluating Redwood Private/Dedicated for in‑app recommendations and search re‑ranking. Main integration concerns you raised:
- Private connectivity (VPC endpoints / PrivateLink) vs. public egress and IP allowlists
- SDK auth and routing for internal services (service-to-service calls)
- mTLS for mutual authentication and cert management
- DNS and egress/static IPs for firewall allowlisting
- Structured output/tool-calling + embeddings/rewriter inference patterns (for later session)

Answers / immediate notes:
- We support Private connectivity via AWS PrivateLink when using our Managed Private offering, and our Redwood Private package can be deployed directly into your VPC if you want full control.
- For hosting models in Dedicated, we can provide predictable egress IPs (Elastic IPs/NAT configuration) to support allowlists, or you can terminate at an internal NLB.
- mTLS is supported for customer-facing endpoints; we can share runbooks for cert rotation and KMS integration.
- SDK: our official SDK supports custom endpoints and hostname overrides; you can point it at internal DNS when using PrivateLink or an internal load balancer.

Attachments: network_diagram_v1.png — rough depiction of where Redwood would sit in your network (attached).

Next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra architect (Soojin Lee) — 60 min to validate network design and gaps. Please share 2 time options this week.
2) Send over a short network requirements spreadsheet (VPC CIDRs, existing proxies, egress constraints) — I attached a template we can fill out if helpful.
3) We'll prepare a short note on auth options: API key vs. mTLS vs. IAM + KMS recommendations and expected operational impacts.

Would Thursday 3/5 10:00am PT or Thursday 3/5 2:00pm PT work for the deep-dive?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Thanks Aditya — good recap. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) PrivateLink vs. Private deploy: If we go Hosted PrivateLink, can you confirm whether traffic to Redwood still egress to a public subnet on your side? We need guarantees around data paths for compliance.
2) Static outbound IPs: we need a small set of static IPs to add to our firewall. Are Elastic IPs supported for Dedicated / Private? If so, what is the expected SLA/availability model?
3) mTLS: do you support client cert auth end-to-end, and do you require us to manage cert rotation or can Redwood handle rotation via our KMS/HSM?
4) SDK: our services are internal-only and will call Redwood from private subnets that route via NAT. Can the SDK resolve an internal DNS name (i.e., when PrivateLink is provisioned) and will bearer tokens/API keys still work over that path?

I attached a short network inventory (customer_network_requirements.xlsx) with our VPC ranges and current egress model — can you confirm if that looks compatible?

Prefer the Thu 3/5 2:00pm PT slot for the deep-dive.

Hi all — quick technical answers ahead of the Thu session. Happy to deep-dive on Thu 3/5 2:00pm PT.

PrivateLink vs Hosted Private deploy:
- Hosted PrivateLink: we publish a service using AWS PrivateLink; customer traffic terminates in our VPC endpoint service. Data paths are inside AWS fabric; for compliance we provide a network topology diagram and flow logs. No public Internet traversal between endpoints when using PrivateLink.
- Redwood Private (customer-deployed): we can deliver a deployable package (helm chart/AMI) that runs entirely in your VPC — you keep full control of network paths and egress.

Static outbound IPs / allowlisting:
- Dedicated deployments: we can provision static Elastic IPs for outbound NAT (or NAT gateway in your VPC for customer-deployed Private). This is the recommended approach for strict allowlist requirements.
- Hosted PrivateLink: outbound IPs from our backend may be shared — if you need static outbound IPs we recommend Dedicated with reserved egress or customer-deployed Private so you control EIPs.

mTLS and cert rotation:
- We support mTLS for client authentication. Two deployment patterns: (1) Customer-managed certs (you provide CA and certs; you handle rotation), or (2) Redwood-managed integration where we integrate with your KMS/HSM for cert storage and can automate rotation via a short-lived cert workflow. We will detail ops/runbook options.

SDK and routing:
- Our SDK supports custom endpoints, hostname overrides, and will work over internal DNS names created for PrivateLink or internal NLBs. API keys and short-lived tokens function identical over private paths; we recommend short-lived tokens (JWT with STS) for improved security.

Recommended pre-reads / links:
- Private connectivity runbook: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-connectivity
- Architecture runbook (design examples): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_architecture-runbook

Info we need from FastRetail before the session:
- VPC CIDRs and whether PrivateLink endpoints are allowed/blocked by policy
- Whether you need static egress IPs or can accept Dedicated with EIPs
- Preferred auth model (mTLS vs short-lived tokens + KMS)
- Expected RPS and peak throughput for inference (so we size the dedicated/Private plan)

I will bring a sample cert rotation playbook and a short diagram showing where mTLS is terminated in each deployment model.

See you Thu 3/5 2pm PT.

—Soojin
